newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares resume climb, industrials lead at open.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares resume climb, industrials lead at open.

text.p: Greek shares resumed their climb early on Monday on the back of Friday's 0.29 percent correction following a streak of 14 rising sessions.
Brokers said market momentum would only allow short-lived corrections.
The Athens general index was trading 0.83 percent or 13.52 points higher to 1,652.31 from Friday's close of 1,638.79 after 25 minutes of trading.
Industrials were leading the market with a 1.78 percent advance, followed by construction and banks which were up 1.43 and 0.57 percent respectively.
Analysts said inflow of funds due to falling interest rates was building up sufficient demand in heavyweight banks and industrials to offset major price corrections.

"The drop in interest rates is channelling funds into equities. The 1,700 level will be attained within the coming fortnight or so, with banks leading the market and industrials following closely," said George Kissandrakis, analyst at Northern Greece Securities.
Brokers cited positive corporate results as further reasons for the sustained rise.

"The uptrend is sustainable in the light of expectations for positive corporate results. Bank stocks will remain in investors' focus, while the outlook for the construction sector is improving," said Telesis Securities in its daily market report.
In a technical outlook, Omega Securities saw the index climbing, albeit at a slower pace than recently.

"For the near-term, we believe the index will drift sideways with a slight upward bias, possibly testing the (historic high) 1,684 level as the medium-term trend expressed by the price oscillator is bullish."
The magnitude of any price correction in the near future was not expected to be considerable.
"A correction of some 50 points is unlikely to take place as any hesitation in prices is seen as a buying opportunity by inverstors," said Kissandrakis.
Turnover amounted to 4.9 billion drachmas on 1.3 million shares traded. Advancing stocks beat decliners 121 to 51 with 15 stocks unchanged on 187 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted unchanged at 1,093-1,123. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were up 10 drachmas at 6,515.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $88.56-$90.26. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,748-3,975.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $22.09-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 288-321 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
